thunderstorms will persist at Pohnpei through Friday afternoon with 
numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms expected through much of 
the weekend. Locally heavy showers will be possible. Combined seas of
6 to 7 feet will persist over the next couple of days before falling
to around 5 feet as we head into next week. Seas consist mostly of a
west swell, a northeast swell, and a southeast swell. Otherwise, 
elevated surf along west-facing will likely continue through at least
Saturday.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will continue through 
tonight at Kosrae before becoming numerous briefly on Friday and 
dropping back to high-end scattered Friday night. Locally heavy 
rainfall will be possible on Friday. Scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms will then persist through at least Saturday with 
shower coverage then dropping back to isolated on Sunday. Southwest 
winds will be mostly moderate over the next two days, before becoming
gentle to moderate late this weekend. The Small Craft Advisory for 
the coastal waters was allowed to expire this afternoon as winds have 
fallen below advisory criteria of sustained 22 knot winds and/or 
frequent gusts to 25 knots. Combined seas of 5 to 6 feet will persist
through Saturday and become 4 to 5 feet on Sunday. Seas consist 
mostly of a west swell, a northeast swell, and a south swell.

Wet and unsettled weather will likely continue at Majuro through 
Friday with high-end scattered to numerous showers and isolated 
thunderstorms expected. Locally heavy showers will be possible.
Shower coverage should then diminish slightly to mostly low-end
scattered showers by late this weekend. Moderate west-northwest 
winds will gradually diminish tonight and into Friday, becoming 
mostly light to gentle by Friday night. Though, portions of the 
southern coastal waters may continue to experience periods of 
moderate winds. Combined seas of around 5 to 6 feet will fall a foot
or so over the next day and become 4 to 5 feet this weekend. Seas
consist of a northeast swell and a southeast swell.

Western Micronesia...
A ridge remains firmly in place over Palau, and is still inducing 
some diffluent flow, leading to quiet conditions over the next a day
or two. Overall, a fairly dry pattern is expected to remain through 
Saturday. Then, the monsoon disturbance, that is currently south of 
Guam, is expected to move into the Philippine seas. This may produce 
showers, bringing some much needed rain to Palau.

A broad monsoon circulation is producing the showers along its 
western flank near Yap Proper's coastal water, however, the ridge to 
the west is making it difficult for these showers to move into the 
region. This circulation is expected to move west-northwest into the 
Philippine seas. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are
expected through Friday. The weekend however, is anticipated to dry 
out as another ridge is expected to move in. For the beginning of 
next week, a trough expending from another monsoon circulation may 
bring showers back into the forecast. 

A monsoon disturbance, located northwest of Chuuk, is expected to 
move in a general west-northwest direction and remain fairly 
disorganized, however, the strengthening convergence along the 
southeastern peripheries will be the focus of unsettled weather for 
the region through the remainder of the week. As the disturbance 
shifts west-northwestward, scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms are expected to continue through Sunday at Chuuk. 

Current altimetry data shows combined seas have remained relatively
stable at 2 to 4 feet near Palau and Yap, and 3 to 5 feet at Chuuk.
Winds are expected to be light to gentle in the west building to
gentle to fresh in the east. 

Seas around Chuuk are expected to be choppy however are expected to 
remain below the 22 knot and 10 foot thresholds for Small Craft 
Advisory. These seas are anticipated to begin to start falling as
early as Saturday.
